header.contentDescription: A mountain range as a 3D surface rising and eroding on one clock

drawTextAnchored.text: plates collide and the crust thickens; it goes up at millimetres a year
rain, ice and gravity take it away, faster the higher it gets
a range stops growing when the two rates match - the Himalaya is near it now
removing a kilometre of rock lets the root float up by most of that, so erosion is slow to win
Everest is not the highest a mountain could be - it is where uplift and erosion currently balance.
A range, rising and wearing down
height is the difference between two rates
